# Configuration

## How configuration works

MicroCPipe is driven by two kinds of files, as in dietJuicer:

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `MicroCSamplesheet.txt` (Core), `MicroCMergeSamplesheet.txt` (Merge) | One row per sequencing run / per library to merge |
| `config/MicroCConfig.yaml` | Everything else: reference, formats, alignment parameters, QC cut-offs |

Both workflows read the same config. `--configfile other.yaml` on a launcher
replaces it (the file must be complete). The shipped file is commented line
by line; this chapter is the full reference. No path, name or parameter is
written into the Snakefiles.

```yaml
samplesheet: 'MicroCSamplesheet.txt'
mergeBy: ['Project', 'Cell_Type', 'Bio_Rep', 'Tech_Rep']
merge: {samplesheet: 'MicroCMergeSamplesheet.txt', mergeBy: ['Project', 'Cell_Type', 'Bio_Rep']}
hpcProfile: 'profiles/local'
outputDir: 'output'
genome: 'hg38'
fasta: '/path/to/hg38/BWAIndex/genome.fa'
chromSizes: '/path/to/hg38.chrom.sizes'
notify: {email: '', events: ['start', 'success', 'error'], command: 'mail -s {subject} {email}'}
outputs: ['cool', 'mcool', 'hic']
base_resolution: 1000
resolutions: [1000, 2000, 5000, 10000, 25000, 50000, 100000, 250000, 500000, 1000000]
balance: true
hic_resolutions: [1000, 2000, 5000, 10000, 25000, 50000, 100000, 250000, 500000, 1000000]
juicerTools: 'scripts/juicer_tools_1.22.01.jar'
javaMem: ''
min_mapq: 40
max_inter_align_gap: 30
walks_policy: '5unique'
bwa_flags: '-5SP -T0'
make_bam: true
library_complexity: true
preseq_extrap: 2.1e9
qc_report: true
qc_thresholds: {...}
analysis: []
analysis_resolution: {expected: 10000, compartments: 100000, insulation: 10000, loops: 5000}
insulation_windows: [50000, 100000, 200000]
```

## Samples

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|-----|---------|---------|
| `samplesheet` | `MicroCSamplesheet.txt` | Core samplesheet. Required columns: `Name`, `Read1`, `Read2`, `Sequencing_Directory`, `Seq_Rep`, and every `mergeBy` column |
| `mergeBy` | `['Project', 'Cell_Type', 'Bio_Rep', 'Tech_Rep']` | Columns joined with `_` to name each group (the output prefix). A column left out is merged into the same group: with `Seq_Rep` omitted, sequencing replicates are aligned separately and then merged and deduplicated together |
| `merge.samplesheet` | `MicroCMergeSamplesheet.txt` | Merge samplesheet. Required columns: `pairs` and every `merge.mergeBy` column |
| `merge.mergeBy` | `['Project', 'Cell_Type', 'Bio_Rep']` | Grouping for the Merge workflow; with `Tech_Rep` omitted, technical replicates merge |

Within a group, Core numbers the rows `run1`, `run2`, ... to give each
alignment job its own ID. In the Merge sheet, repeated `pairs` paths within
a group are used once.

### Samplesheet columns

Both sheets are tab-separated text files with a header row.

| Sheet | Column | Required? | Meaning |
|-------|--------|-----------|---------|
| Core | `Name` | yes | Label for the row; not used in file names |
| Core | `Read1`, `Read2` | yes | FASTQ file names |
| Core | `Sequencing_Directory` | yes | Folder holding both files (joined with the file name) |
| Core | `Seq_Rep` | yes | Sequencing replicate number |
| Core, Merge | every column named in `mergeBy` | yes | Metadata that defines groups (default `Project`, `Cell_Type`, `Bio_Rep`, `Tech_Rep`; Merge: no `Tech_Rep`) |
| Merge | `pairs` | yes | Path to a Core `.pairs.gz` |
| both | any other column (`Condition`, ...) | no | Free-form metadata, ignored by the pipeline |

### How `mergeBy` turns rows into groups and file names

Take this Core samplesheet (columns shortened):

```text
Name     Project  Cell_Type  Bio_Rep  Tech_Rep  Seq_Rep  Read1
rowA     Ex       ESC        1        1         1        a_R1.fastq.gz
rowB     Ex       ESC        1        1         2        b_R1.fastq.gz
rowC     Ex       ESC        1        2         1        c_R1.fastq.gz
```

With the default `mergeBy: ['Project', 'Cell_Type', 'Bio_Rep', 'Tech_Rep']`:

| Row | Group (values joined with `_`) | Run ID |
|-----|--------------------------------|--------|
| rowA | `Ex_ESC_1_1` | `Ex_ESC_1_1_run1` |
| rowB | `Ex_ESC_1_1` | `Ex_ESC_1_1_run2` |
| rowC | `Ex_ESC_1_2` | `Ex_ESC_1_2_run1` |

That gives three `align` jobs, two groups, and two sets of outputs:
`output/Ex_ESC_1_1/Ex_ESC_1_1.mcool` (rows A and B merged and deduplicated
together) and `output/Ex_ESC_1_2/Ex_ESC_1_2.mcool`. If you add `Seq_Rep` to
`mergeBy`, all three rows become separate groups (`Ex_ESC_1_1_1`, ...).

The Merge workflow works the same way on its own sheet, but prefixes the group
with `merged_`: with `merge: mergeBy: ['Project', 'Cell_Type', 'Bio_Rep']`, the
Merge rows for `Ex_ESC_1_1` and `Ex_ESC_1_2` (their `pairs` paths) form the
group `merged_Ex_ESC_1`, written to
`output/merged_Ex_ESC_1/merged_Ex_ESC_1.mcool`.

Example of a custom samplesheet and grouping:

```yaml
samplesheet: 'my_samples.txt'
mergeBy: ['Project', 'Cell_Type', 'Condition', 'Bio_Rep']
```

## Compute site and location

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|-----|---------|---------|
| `hpcProfile` | `profiles/local` | Profile folder (`env.sh` + `config.yaml`). Overridden by `--profile`, then `$MICROC_PROFILE` |
| `outputDir` | `output` | Where results go. A relative path is placed under `$MICROC_OUTPUT_ROOT` when set, otherwise under the directory you launch from; an absolute path is used as written |

Example: `hpcProfile: 'profiles/mycluster'` (or leave it and set
`MICROC_PROFILE`); `outputDir: '/path/to/scratch/MicroCPipe/output'` for an
absolute location.

## Reference

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|-----|---------|---------|
| `genome` | `hg38` | Assembly label stored in the `.cool` (`cooler cload --assembly`). It does not select a reference |
| `fasta` | placeholder path | BWA-indexed FASTA for `bwa mem` |
| `chromSizes` | placeholder path | Two columns (name, length). Used by `pairtools parse` (`--chroms-path`), `cooler` (the bins) and `juicer_tools pre`. Every contig listed becomes part of the maps; chromosome names must match the FASTA |

Example (mouse): `genome: 'mm10'`, `fasta: '/path/to/mm10/BWAIndex/genome.fa'`,
`chromSizes: '/path/to/mm10.chrom.sizes'`.

## Email notifications

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|-----|---------|---------|
| `notify.email` | `''` | Address. `$MICROC_EMAIL` wins if set. With neither, nothing is sent |
| `notify.events` | `['start', 'success', 'error']` | Which events send a message. One message per event, never one per job |
| `notify.command` | `mail -s {subject} {email}` | Shell command that sends one message; `{subject}` and `{email}` are filled in (shell-quoted) and the body arrives on stdin |

The error message includes the last 40 lines of the Snakemake log.
Dry runs send nothing, and a failed send is reported on stderr but never
fails the run. See [Running](running.qmd#email-notifications).

Example: `notify: {email: '', events: ['error'], command: 'sendmail {email}'}`
sends only failure messages, using `sendmail`. Prefer `export MICROC_EMAIL=...`
over writing an address into a shared config.

## Output formats

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|-----|---------|---------|
| `outputs` | `['cool', 'mcool', 'hic']` | Any subset of `cool`, `mcool`, `hic`. Anything else stops the run with an error |
| `base_resolution` | `1000` | Bin size (bp) of the `.cool`. The unit all `mcool` resolutions are built from |
| `resolutions` | 1 kb to 1 Mb (10 values) | Resolutions in the `.mcool`. Each must be a multiple of `base_resolution`; the base is added automatically if missing |
| `balance` | `true` | ICE-balance every resolution of the `.mcool` (`cooler zoomify --balance`). The base `.cool` is not balanced. `.hic` files get juicer's own normalisations regardless |
| `hic_resolutions` | same 10 values | Resolutions written to the `.hic` (`juicer_tools pre -r`). Defaults to `resolutions` if the key is absent |
| `juicerTools` | `scripts/juicer_tools_1.22.01.jar` | The jar used for `pre` |
| `javaMem` | `''` | JVM heap (`-Xmx`) for `pre`, e.g. `'96g'`. Empty (the default) means 85% of the `hic` rule's `mem_mb` from the profile, so the heap follows the job's memory. If you set a value, keep it below `mem_mb` |

Requesting `mcool` builds the `.cool` first, since `mcool` is made from it.

Examples: `outputs: ['mcool']` (no `.hic`); `resolutions: [1000, 5000, 10000,
50000, 1000000]`; `hic_resolutions: [5000, 10000, 100000]`; `javaMem: '96g'`
(keep below the `hic` rule's `mem_mb`).

`javaMem` and `hic: mem_mb` are the first things to raise for a deeper
library; see [Choosing resources](cluster.qmd#choosing-resources).

## Alignment and pair parsing

| Key | Default | Passed to |
|-----|---------|-----------|
| `bwa_flags` | `-5SP -T0` | `bwa mem` (Micro-C / Hi-C standard) |
| `min_mapq` | `40` | `pairtools parse --min-mapq` |
| `max_inter_align_gap` | `30` | `pairtools parse --max-inter-align-gap` (bp) |
| `walks_policy` | `5unique` | `pairtools parse --walks-policy` |

Example: `min_mapq: 30` keeps more alignments (a lower value counts more
reads as uniquely mapped); `bwa_flags: '-5SP -T0'` is the Micro-C standard and
rarely needs changing.

## QC

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|-----|---------|---------|
| `make_bam` | `true` | Keep the sorted BAM `{group}_mapped.PT.bam` (+ `.bai`) as a final output. It is also the input to `preseq`, so `library_complexity` needs it |
| `library_complexity` | `true` | Run `preseq lc_extrap` (needs `make_bam`) |
| `preseq_extrap` | `2.1e9` | `preseq -extrap`: how far (in reads) to extrapolate |
| `qc_report` | `true` | Build `output/qc/MicroC_qc_report.html` |
| `qc_thresholds` | see below | Traffic-light cut-offs for the dashboard |

Example: `library_complexity: false` skips preseq and `qc_report: false` skips
the dashboard; `make_bam: false` also skips the BAM and preseq.

`library_complexity` never stops the pipeline: if preseq fails on a very
shallow library, a header-only table is written, a warning goes to the log
(`output/<group>/logs/<group>_preseq.log`), and the dashboard shows no curve
for that sample.

### `qc_thresholds`

Each metric has a `direction` and two edges, `warn` and `fail`. For
`higher_is_better`, a value below `fail` fails and a value below `warn`
warns; for `lower_is_better` the reverse (above `fail` fails, above `warn`
warns).

| Metric | Direction | warn | fail | What it is |
|--------|-----------|------|------|------------|
| `mapped_pct` | higher | 80 | 60 | Mapped read pairs, % |
| `duplicate_pct` | lower | 40 | 60 | Duplicate read pairs, % |
| `cis_pct` | higher | 70 | 50 | Cis pairs, % of non-duplicate pairs |
| `cis_ge1kb_pct` | higher | 40 | 25 | Cis pairs >= 1 kb, % of non-duplicate pairs |
| `cis_lt1kb_pct` | lower | 40 | 55 | Cis pairs < 1 kb, % of non-duplicate pairs |
| `cis_ge10kb_pct` | higher | 20 | 10 | Cis pairs >= 10 kb, % of non-duplicate pairs |
| `unique_pairs_million` | higher | 100 | 20 | Non-duplicate pairs, millions (absolute) |

These are starting points chosen for this pipeline, not published
standards. Library type, cell type and protocol all shift them, so adjust
the edges to what your good libraries look like. The dashboard reads them
from the config file the run was started with (`--configfile`, else
`config/MicroCConfig.yaml`); after editing, rebuild with
`bash MicroCPipe.sh --forcerun qc_report`.

Example: to warn earlier about shallow libraries,
`unique_pairs_million: {direction: higher_is_better, warn: 50, fail: 10}`.
The list you write **replaces** the shipped one: a metric you leave out is not
shown or judged, and a metric name the dashboard does not know has no value.
Copy the whole block from the shipped config and edit numbers.

## Optional downstream analysis

::: {.callout-note}
**Tested on one real dataset.** Each option ran and produced output on a
25M-pair mouse library (one dataset, one cluster). They are off by default, and
the results have not been validated biologically: at that depth `loops` called
only 10 loops with default settings. Check the output against your expectations.
:::

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|-----|---------|---------|
| `analysis` | `[]` | Any of `expected` (`cooltools expected-cis`), `compartments` (`cooltools eigs-cis`), `insulation` (`cooltools insulation`), `loops` (`mustache`). Each runs on the `.mcool` and writes into `output/{group}/analysis/` |
| `analysis_resolution` | `expected: 10000`, `compartments: 100000`, `insulation: 10000`, `loops: 5000` | Resolution (bp) used by each; must be in `resolutions` |
| `insulation_windows` | `[50000, 100000, 200000]` | Window sizes (bp) for `insulation` |

The `.mcool` is built as a dependency even when `mcool` is not in `outputs`. `compartments` and `insulation` read
the balanced weights, so keep `balance: true` (see
[Recipes](recipes.qmd#add-a-downstream-analysis)).

Example: `analysis: ['expected', 'insulation']` with
`analysis_resolution: {expected: 10000, insulation: 10000}`. `loops` uses its
own conda environment, `envs/microc_mustache.yml`.

## Environment variables

| Variable | Used by | Meaning |
|----------|---------|---------|
| `MICROC_PROFILE` | launchers, `unlock.sh` | Profile folder; beats `hpcProfile`, loses to `--profile` |
| `MICROC_OUTPUT_ROOT` | every rule, launchers | Folder a relative `outputDir` goes under |
| `MICROC_EMAIL` | both workflows | Notification address; beats `notify.email` |
| `MICROC_CONDA_ROOT` | `profiles/*/env.sh` | Miniforge install, if not `$HOME/miniforge3` |

Also standard, not MicroCPipe-specific: `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, `CONDA_PKGS_DIRS` and `PIP_CACHE_DIR` move caches off a small home directory ([Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.qmd#moving-caches-to-scratch)).
